payload.rationale:
To resolve to YES, the 2026 annual average must be strictly greater than both the 2025 value (1.19 C) and 1.28 C. Therefore, the target is > 1.28 C. The sum of the anomalies for the first eight months (Jan-Aug) is 9.79 C, which averages to approximately 1.224 C. To achieve an annual average > 1.28 C, the total sum for the 12 months must exceed 15.36 C. This means the remaining four months (Sep-Dec) must sum to at least 5.57 C, requiring an average of approximately 1.393 C per month. 

The strongest reason the estimate could be too low is the presence of a strengthening El Niño, which has a >90% chance of becoming a very strong event in the fall and winter of 2026-27. August 2026 already reached 1.40 C, demonstrating that anomalies in this range are possible as the El Niño peaks. 

The strongest reason the estimate could be too high is that sustaining an average of ~1.39 C over four consecutive months is a very high bar. Prior to August, the highest monthly anomaly in 2026 was 1.32 C, and most months were well below 1.30 C. Any slight dip in the anomaly trend would make the 1.28 C annual threshold mathematically unreachable. Thus, while possible, it remains an uphill climb.
limitations: The exact trajectory of the strengthening El Niño and its immediate impact on global surface temperatures for the final four months is uncertain.
No probabilistic model or historical distribution of late-year El Niño temperature spikes is provided.
Revisions to the Jan-Aug data could alter the required threshold for the remaining months.
